questions.stem:
For a reaction $\mathrm{A \xrightarrow{K_1} B \xrightarrow{K_2} C}$
If the rate of formation of B is set to be zero then the concentration of B is given by :
questions.solution:
Rate of formation of B is
$$\frac{d[B]}{dt} = k_1[A] - k_2[B]$$
$0 = k_1[A] - k_2[B]$
$$\left(\frac{k_1}{k_2}\right)[A] = [B]$$

questions.stem: When $\psi_A$ and $\Psi_B$ are the wave functions of atomic orbitals, then $\sigma^{*}$ is represented by :

Antibonding molecular orbitals are formed by destructive interference of wave functions.
(ABMO) $\sigma^{*} = \psi_A - \psi_B$

questions.stem: The emf of cell $\mathrm{Tl\,|\,Tl^{+}\,(0.001\,M)\,\|\,Cu^{2+}\,(0.01\,M)\,|\,Cu}$ is 0.83 V at 298 K. It could be increased by :
questions.solution:
Anodic Reaction: $\mathrm{[Tl_{(s)} \rightarrow Tl^{+}_{(aq)} + e^{-}]} \times 2$
Cathodic Reaction: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}_{(aq)} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow Cu_{(s)}}$
Overall Redox Reaction: $\mathrm{2Tl_{(s)} + Cu^{2+}_{(aq)} \rightarrow 2Tl^{+}_{(aq)} + Cu_{(s)}}$
$$E_{cell} = E^{o}_{cell} - \frac{0.0591}{2}\log\frac{[\mathrm{Tl^{+}}]^{2}}{[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}]}$$
$E_{cell}$ increases by increasing concentration of $[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}]$ ions.

options.text: increasing concentration of both $\mathrm{Tl^{+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ions
decreasing concentration of both $\mathrm{Tl^{+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ions

questions.stem:
Identify the correct statements about p-block elements and their compounds.
(A) Non metals have higher electronegativity than metals.
(B) Non metals have lower ionisation enthalpy than metals.
(C) Compounds formed between highly reactive nonmetals and highly reactive metals are generally ionic.
(D) The non-metal oxides are generally basic in nature.
(E) The metal oxides are generally acidic or neutral in nature.
questions.solution:
As electronegativity increases non-metallic nature increases.
Along the period ionisation energy increases.
High electronegativity difference results in ionic bond formation.
Oxides of metals are generally basic and that of non-metals are acidic in nature.

questions.stem:
$\Delta_{vap}H^{\ominus}$ for water is $+40.49\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ at 1 bar and $100^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Change in internal energy for this vapourisation under same condition is ______ $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. (Integer answer)
(Given $R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{H_2O(\ell) \rightleftharpoons H_2O(g)}$   $\Delta H^{0}_{vap} = 40.79\ \mathrm{kJ/mole}$
$\Delta H^{0}_{vap} = \Delta U^{0}_{vap} + \Delta n_g RT$
$$40.79 = \Delta U^{0}_{vap} + \frac{1 \times 8.3 \times 373.15}{1000}$$
$\Delta U^{0}_{vap} = 40.79 - 3.0971$
$= 37.6929$
$\Delta U^{0}_{vap} = 38$

questions.stem:
A solution is prepared by adding 1 mole ethyl alcohol in 9 mole water. The mass percent of solute in the solution is _______ (Integer Answer)
(Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$ Ethyl alcohol : 46, water : 18)
questions.solution:
Mass percent of Alcohol
$$= \frac{\text{Mass of ethyl alcohol}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 100$$
$$= \frac{1 \times 46}{1 \times 46 + 9 \times 18} \times 100 = \frac{4600}{208}$$
$= 22.11$ Or 22
